criteria.criterion: The push-first loop converges after five deterministic competing pushes: five in-loop pushes are each followed by fetch+merge only on retriable rejection, then exactly one terminal sixth push spends the fifth clean merge. The oracle pins six total pushes in that case, pins no terminal push after earlier success, introduces no duplicate final push, and selects semantic branches without navigating by source line number.

Every strict core failure branch raises the reusable catchable `PushDeliveryError`; core never calls `sys.exit`, and paired core-boundary tests assert the pinned reason vocabulary (`push-disabled`, `async-delivery-unobservable`, `invalid-destination`, `remote-not-found`, `push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `merge-recovery-blocked`, `store-epoch-pre-merge`, `store-epoch-during-recovery`, `final-push-rejected`, `lock-timeout`) and unpushed count.

The private module `push` action is the sole process boundary translating `PushDeliveryError` to nonzero plus stderr, proven by a real subprocess test; dependent child 2bc9 reuses and extends this adapter.
Strict `off`, `async`, malformed destination, and missing remote configurations fail explicitly.
Every paired best-effort case returns normally and preserves local commits and working-tree state.

A parametrized caller-contract test covers event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim; every site omits strict delivery (or reaches core with `strict=False`), preserves its legacy best-effort return/disposition contract, and inherits only the five-cycle plus exactly-one-final-push durability correction.
Strict failure writes no ticket event and never emits `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
Existing narrow-refspec, stash/pop, epoch-guard, and rejection-classification contracts remain green.

`docs/concurrency.md` distinguishes the unchanged default best-effort contract from opt-in strict delivery, documents the pinned `PushDeliveryError` reason vocabulary (including policy-decline versus transport-failure), and states that all existing callers remain best-effort while inheriting only the five-attempt plus terminal-push durability correction.
